log.tx: Robots pack the kits now. Your packers are looked after.
Kiki has watched the machines since 2029. The packing line jammed at 3 am. Kiki was there.
Your cousin has run a region since 2029. A shrimp company’s regional manager promises a mall chain kits it doesn’t have. The chain cancels.
AI agents take over sales. 1 salespeople move on.
The kit price war is over. The rival cut in 3 of 12 months. You never did.
You sent the farm crew to drill since 2031. A shrimp farm’s crew drilled three new wells for the town upriver.
Wild cherry shrimp are back in the Taiwan streams. Kids catch them with nets and let them go.
Indian almond trees are coming up in backyards all over town. Owners dry the leaves for their shrimp.
Your farms sell their spare power to the grid. A wind farm in Inner Mongolia joins next spring.
Fund it, publish whatever they find (2031). The shrimp and stress study is out. Watching shrimp really does calm people down, a little.

Your neighbors on the coast road start planting mangroves too. Nobody pays them to.
A local paper runs “Who is the person behind the kits?” on its front page. Nobody at the kit shop will say.
When shrimp die in an owner’s tank, they buy a bag of ten for AED 40 to fill it back up. Your farms have shrimp to spare, so that’s money every day.

dlog.t: The shrimp club makes you treasurer. Everyone knows someone.
In a tank trial, peppermint cleaner shrimp removed up to 98% of some parasites from farmed fish (Vaughan et al., 2018).
You’re elected president of the shrimp club. The mayor comes to the meetings now.
Spiny lobsters show who’s in charge with chemicals in their pee. Block the signal and their fights get worse (Shabani et al., 2009).
Young Amano shrimp walk up from the sea into rivers at night, sometimes up almost vertical wet walls (Hamano & Hayashi, 1992).
Some mantis shrimp have 12 kinds of color receptor and still can’t tell apart colors people can (Thoen et al., 2014).
Some cleaner shrimp kept in threes or fours fought until only two were left alive (Wong & Michiels, 2011).
Some shrimp live in colonies of over 300 relatives, one breeding female and the rest of the family defending the colony (Duffy, 1996).
Some cherry shrimp are bolder than others, and part of it is in their genes (Wilson et al., 2026).
Some reef fish turn darker to ask for a cleaning, and cleaner shrimp wave their antennae to say they’re open (Caves et al., 2018).
Shrimp ponds caused about 31% of the world’s mangrove loss in 2000 to 2010, and 21% the decade after (FAO, 2023).
White, red and brown cherry shrimp all picked dark ground in a test, even when it made them stand out (Plichta et al., 2021).
Hermit crabs take stronger electric shocks before they leave a shell they like. They weigh one thing against another (Appel & Elwood, 2009).
Some mantis shrimp see circularly polarized light, which people can’t, and use it to stay out of burrows that might be taken (Gagnon et al., 2015).
Some deep-sea shrimp feed on bacteria living in their gill chambers, taking in what the bacteria make through their skin (Ponsard et al., 2013).
Crayfish remember the faces of crayfish they’ve fought before and tell them apart from strangers (Van der Velden et al., 2008).
Amano shrimp live in fresh water as adults, but their larvae need salt water to grow up (Kondo et al., 2021).
Shrimp at deep-sea vents have light-sensing organs on their backs, under a clear shell, in place of normal eyes (Van Dover et al., 1989).
Sleeping crayfish show slow brain waves and react less to what’s around them, a sleep-like state (Ramón et al., 2004).
In one stream experiment, freshwater shrimp cleared all the silt off the test surfaces in 30 minutes (Pringle et al., 1993).
Some of the most colorful cleaner shrimp see in low resolution and may not see their own colors (Caves et al., 2016).
Young female cherry shrimp mature faster when they can touch males. Seeing or smelling them from a distance doesn’t do it (Tropea et al., 2018).
After a stressful experience crayfish turn cautious, and a drug used for anxiety in people undoes it. The paper calls it anxiety-like (Fossat et al., 2014).
A pistol shrimp’s claw makes a bubble that collapses at 5,000 K or more, hot enough to give a tiny flash of light (Lohse et al., 2001).
Shrimp smell food from far off with their antennae, then taste it with their legs and mouthparts before they eat (Eap et al., 2020).
A study in Philippine mangroves found thousands of young shrimp living among the roots (Primavera, 1998).

After a stressful experience crayfish turn cautious, and a drug used for anxiety in people undoes it. The paper calls it anxiety-like (Fossat et al., 2014).
Some deep-sea shrimp feed on bacteria living in their gill chambers, taking in what the bacteria make through their skin (Ponsard et al., 2013).
The marine survey
Some reef fish turn darker to ask for a cleaning, and cleaner shrimp wave their antennae to say they’re open (Caves et al., 2018).
Shrimpcoin
Shrimp smell food from far off with their antennae, then taste it with their legs and mouthparts before they eat (Eap et al., 2020).
A pistol shrimp’s claw makes a bubble that collapses at 5,000 K or more, hot enough to give a tiny flash of light (Lohse et al., 2001).
Crayfish remember the faces of crayfish they’ve fought before and tell them apart from strangers (Van der Velden et al., 2008).
Hermit crabs take stronger electric shocks before they leave a shell they like. They weigh one thing against another (Appel & Elwood, 2009).
The permit
Some mantis shrimp have 12 kinds of color receptor and still can’t tell apart colors people can (Thoen et al., 2014).
Sleeping crayfish show slow brain waves and react less to what’s around them, a sleep-like state (Ramón et al., 2004).
Shrimp ponds caused about 31% of the world’s mangrove loss in 2000 to 2010, and 21% the decade after (FAO, 2023).
Some of the most colorful cleaner shrimp see in low resolution and may not see their own colors (Caves et al., 2016).
In one stream experiment, freshwater shrimp cleared all the silt off the test surfaces in 30 minutes (Pringle et al., 1993).
White, red and brown cherry shrimp all picked dark ground in a test, even when it made them stand out (Plichta et al., 2021).
Some mantis shrimp see circularly polarized light, which people can’t, and use it to stay out of burrows that might be taken (Gagnon et al., 2015).
The hatchery bust
Young female cherry shrimp mature faster when they can touch males. Seeing or smelling them from a distance doesn’t do it (Tropea et al., 2018).
Some shrimp live in colonies of over 300 relatives, one breeding female and the rest of the family defending the colony (Duffy, 1996).
Some cleaner shrimp kept in threes or fours fought until only two were left alive (Wong & Michiels, 2011).
Shrimp at deep-sea vents have light-sensing organs on their backs, under a clear shell, in place of normal eyes (Van Dover et al., 1989).
In a tank trial, peppermint cleaner shrimp removed up to 98% of some parasites from farmed fish (Vaughan et al., 2018).
